title: Flat morphisms give stalkwise Tor independence
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a flat morphism of schemes [def-weil-flat-morphism], and let $g:T\to S$ be any scheme morphism. For every $x\in X$, $t\in T$ with $f(x)=g(t)$, and every $i>0$, the module $\operatorname{Tor}_i^{\mathcal O_{S,f(x)}}(\mathcal O_{X,x},\mathcal O_{T,t})$ is zero, with the actual stalk-map scalar structures and the base-point transport of [def-pc-pullback-stalk-tensor-comparison].

source.place: Tag 00M3 (Tor symmetry); perfect.tex, Tags 08IB and 0AA7, case (1) (application to scheme base change)

proof.text:
the left stalk is flat over the base stalk by the stalk criterion for flat
morphisms. By symmetry of Tor, resolve the other stalk by projectives and tensor
with the flat left stalk. Tensoring preserves the exactness of the resolution
in positive degrees. Its positive homology is therefore zero. Transport through
Tor symmetry and the projective-resolution computation of Tor. This applies to
all pairs over the same base point; the right stalk's transported scalar action
requires no flatness assumption. For an empty scheme there are no such pairs.
